Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (obs), Maya Lopez (CTO - HavenPoint), Ben Carter (Lead SRE), Anya Singh (ML Eng), Derek Yu (Security)
Recorded with Fireflies.ai
summary: Technical deep dive focused on console tracing and request-level forensics. Walked through a simulated failure path, KV cache fallbacks, traceback mapping, and how to correlate request logs with model-level events. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a pilot: hosted API first, then Dedicated/VPC for PHI-sensitive flows. Action items: share SOC2/KMS docs, run benchmark trace, provide pilot scope and sample traffic.
topics: Error analysis and root cause playbook
transcript:
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Evan from Redwood, AE. We'll do a quick intros then Priya will jump into the console -- the request path, traces, error hunting playbook.
[00:08] Maya: Hi all, Maya here. Trying to understand how we would debug intermittent 502s we see spiking at night.
[00:12] Ben: Ben from SRE, yeah the patterns look like timeouts or cache misses but not sure.
[00:18] Priya: Great. Quick agenda: 1) repro of a failure path, 2) live trace inspection, 3) KV cache fallback drill, 4) what you get in logs + links to artifacts. We'll also call out security/SSO notes.
[00:30] Priya: Alright pulling up the Console now — sorry there's a little UI lag on my side — okay, so here's the request inspector, you can see a request timeline on the right, token-level latency, and model variant routing.
[00:40] Ben: That token-level heatmap, is that per-model or aggregated?
[00:44] Priya: per-request per-model. The trace groups all sub-operations. Sometimes the label says 'runtine' instead of 'runtime' — the transcript captioning sometimes mislabels but the data is accurate.
[00:55] [00:55] Evan: Quick note — we recorded a sample workload you sent, Priya loaded it into the sandbox, so we'll walk through the same pattern you saw.
[01:05] Priya: Here's a request that failed at 02:15 UTC. The timeline shows a spike at decoder step 7, then a fallback to smaller quantized variant.
[01:15] Anya: Wait, fallback to quantized? I thought fallbacks were only region/variant not quantization.
[01:20] Priya: Good call — it's a compatible variant fallback we configured: when KV cache invalidations occur the runtime can route to a low-memory quantized variant as a graceful degrade. That can increase token time but reduce OOM.
[01:31] Derek: From a compliance perspective, where does the KV cache live for Dedicated versus Hosted?
[01:36] Evan: In Hosted it's in our managed cache with encryption at rest, Dedicated gives you an isolated pool in your VPC and you control KMS keys if you want. We'll share the KMS note after.
[01:46] [02:00] Priya: Okay digging into the trace — you see the sequence: request received -> prefix hit check -> KV lookup -> small batch exec -> model exec -> token stream. The error bubble shows a 'net read timeout' then a retry that used another route.
[02:18] Ben: Do you keep full request payloads in logs? We need to be mindful of PHI.
[02:22] Evan: By default we mask and retention is configurable. For Private deployments you can opt out of cloud logging; audit logs are available to your SIEM.
[02:30] Priya: I'm going to open the raw request log — note the correlation id in the top-right, you can copy to clipboard and paste into the trace search.
[02:45] [03:00] Priya: Here the initial KV lookup returned a 404 — that's a cache miss — then we attempted a direct model call which hit a sequence length spike and small OOM, so the runtime retried with a quantized variant. That retry succeeded but latency spiked.
[03:20] Anya: That matches the ~1.8s spikes we saw. Can you show the per-token timings?
[03:25] Priya: Yep. Token 1-6 are <20ms, token 7 jumps to 600ms — that's where the kernel selection changed. Sometimes the kernel selector misestimates memory for mixed-precision layers.
[03:40] Evan: This is why we recommend a canary that hits tail behaviors — small amounts of long context or token-level adversarial inputs.
[03:48] Maya: How do we capture these tail traces without sending PHI?
[03:52] Priya: Two options: 1) synthetic traffic that reproduces shapes, or 2) you can scrub PII client-side and send correlation ids. We can also run a local profiler in Private mode.
[04:05] [04:15] Ben: Show us the fallback config — where do we set thresholds?
[04:18] Priya: In the policy tab. Here: latency SLO, OOM threshold, route priority. You can configure fallback to warmed quantized pool or to a cheaper region.
[04:30] Priya: Also important — there's an automatic KV cache invalidation window. If your data pipeline produces TTLs less than that, you'll see frequent misses.
[04:45] Anya: Our TTLs are 30s sometimes, due to live content. That could explain churn.
[04:50] Priya: Yup, short TTLs cause cache thrash which magnifies cold start effects. We can show memory footprint and batching impact next.
[05:00] [05:12] Evan: Quick interruption — Competitor note: some vendors don't expose token-level timings or correlation ids which makes this much harder. We try to give you the full stack traces with links to raw logs.
[05:22] Maya: Can you link the trace to the console alert we configured? We got a paged alert at 02:16.
[05:27] Priya: Yes. Alerts tie to traces. In Alerts config you can attach a diagnostic bundle that includes the last 5 traces for the call id, model variant history, and a CPU/MEM snapshot.
[05:40] Ben: Do those bundles include stack traces from the runtime?
[05:44] Priya: They include runtime error codes and kernel failures, not low-level vendor stack by default. For Dedicated we can enable extended debug logging.
[05:55] [06:00] Priya: I'm going to demo the 'request path replay' — we can re-ingest a recorded request into sandbox to step through the KV hits and kernel decisions. Starting replay now.
[06:12] Evan: Note — replay is rate-limited in Hosted sandboxes to avoid noisy replays affecting others. We'll give you a dedicated replay slot for the pilot.
[06:20] [06:35] Priya: Replay got the same token spike at step 7. Looking at the kernel chooser, it selected a fallback kernel due to an estimated memory budget overshoot. There's a heuristic threshold that sometimes errs on smaller batches.
[06:50] Anya: Is the heuristic observable? Can we tune it per model?
[06:54] Priya: You can set model profiles and preferred kernel hints; SEs can push tuned profiles to the runtime. For the pilot we'll include a tuned profile for your top two generation tasks.
[07:08] Derek: On encryption: if we use customer-managed keys, how is key rotation handled with the cache?
[07:15] Evan: KMS rotations are supported; cache is encrypted with envelope keys so rotation doesn't require cache invalidation. We'll provide KMS integration notes.
[07:26] [07:40] Priya: Back to the logs — see this scatter of small timeouts right before the spike, likely network jitter on the inference plane. There's a 'net_read_timeout' at 02:14:58 and a retry 02:15:02.
[07:52] Ben: That pattern also showed up on our infra monitor — a noisy NIC on one host. If the runtime retries across hosts, that could mask it.
[07:58] Priya: Exactly — our smart routing will reroute to another replica which can mask the underlying infra issue but increase latency.
[08:12] Maya: For canary testing, what's the suggested traffic percentage to catch this?
[08:16] Evan: We typically recommend 0.1-1% of production for tail behavior with extended sampling and trace retention for at least 7 days during the canary.
[08:26] [08:40] Priya: I'm going to show an example of an error playbook. Step 1: correlate alert to trace via correlation id. Step 2: check prefix/KV hit rates. Step 3: inspect kernel selection and batch sizes. Step 4: if it's infra, escalate to host metrics, else adjust fallback thresholds or model profile.
[08:58] Ben: Can we automate some of those checks?
[09:02] Priya: Yes, Console supports runbooks that automatically collect diagnostic bundles and run a triage script that outputs probable root causes. You can add custom checks.
[09:12] Anya: Does the triage script surface quantization regressions?
[09:16] Priya: It will flag variant switches and compare output similarity scores; Redwood Optimize can run quality regressions across prompts too.
[09:26] [09:40] Evan: Quick aside — some of our customers use Optimize to pick quantization profiles that hit a sweet spot between latency and quality, we can include Optimize trial for your pilot.
[09:50] Maya: Good. From a procurement lens, we'll need a security pack and SLA. Derek will follow up.
[09:56] Derek: Yep, need SOC2, encryption, SSO. Also ask about logging retention controls.
[10:02] Evan: We'll attach our security packet after — SOC2, ISO summary, KMS approach, and retention controls.
[10:10] [10:20] Priya: Back to the replay — I want to demonstrate a 'root cause hypothesis' view. It summarizes three candidate causes: cache thrash (60% likelihood), kernel mis-estimation (25%), infra jitter (15%). You can click to expand supporting traces.
[10:36] Ben: How does it estimate those percentages?
[10:40] Priya: Heuristics plus ML models trained on historical failure patterns; we keep that tunable and transparent.
[10:48] Anya: Are those models open to customer data? Like, can we feed our previous incidents?
[10:52] Priya: For Dedicated we can include tenant-only training data to improve accuracy. For hosted it's aggregate unless you opt into private training.
[11:06] [11:20] Priya: Now I'm going to trigger a simulated cache miss storm. You should see a flood of 404s and then increased retries. Running script...
[11:32] Anya: I'm watching the trace stream. The retry rate increased to 3x and latency tail jumped.
[11:40] Priya: Console aggregates that into a 'failure storm' event and surfaces affected routes and models so you can scope the blast radius.
[11:50] Ben: Can rollback be automated? Like, automatically switch to a more conservative variant when storm detected?
[11:54] Priya: Yes, policy engine can automatically fallback to a pinned variant or route to another region, and it can throttle traffic or divert to a degraded quality path.
[12:05] Maya: For PHI we probably want to avoid cross-region fallback. Can that be blocked?
[12:09] Priya: Absolutely — routing policies can include region constraints and data residency rules.
[12:16] [12:30] Evan: Let's talk about the audit trail — every action in the Console is logged with who did it, old/new policy, and a diff. That shows up in the audit log export for your SIEM.
[12:44] Derek: Are audit logs tamper-resistant?
[12:48] Evan: They're append-only and can be shipped to your cloud logs or HSM-backed storage. We'll include details in the security packet.
[12:56] Priya: Switching back — I want to highlight the 'token inspector' plugin. You can replay per-token model outputs to inspect hallucination triggers next to the kernel events.
[13:08] Anya: That will help our evals team. Do we need to keep full outputs?
[13:12] Priya: You can configure retention and redaction — outputs can be hashed or redacted at ingestion.
[13:20] [13:30] Ben: On scaling: if we enable dedicated pools, does the console still show the same traces?
[13:34] Priya: Yes same Console. Dedicated pools appear as separate capacity with their own KPIs and trace IDs still correlate across the control plane.
[13:44] Maya: Great. Can we simulate a Dedicated-like environment in sandbox for debugging?
[13:48] Priya: We'll provision an isolated sandbox that mimics Dedicated behavior including KMS integration for the pilot.
[13:56] [14:10] Priya: Now a quick Q on root cause artifacts — here's a download link for a diagnostic bundle (link: https://app.redwood.example/diag/ff-demo-20261207) - this is a demo link only.
[14:22] Anya: Received. I'll feed it to our incident parser.
[14:28] Priya: Note some fields in the log like 'kv_key' are hashed in hosted mode, but in the private bundle they will include full keys if you opt-in.
[14:40] Ben: How do we correlate our internal trace ids with Redwood correlation ids?
[14:44] Evan: You can push your correlation id in the request header x-haven-id or we can map via webhook. Then Console will show both IDs in the same trace.
[14:56] [15:10] Priya: Next I want to walk through a 'request forensic' we saved. Opening: you can see the complete timeline, the model variant history, and the batch sizes.
[15:22] Priya: There's an interesting bit — 3rd retry had a different model version pinned by a rollout policy. That rollout was scheduled earlier that night.
[15:32] Maya: Oh! So rollout timing coincided with our high traffic window. Could be the cause.
[15:36] Ben: Did the rollout enforce canary percentages?
[15:40] Priya: Yes 5% canary but because of low traffic from a small pool the canary routed to the same nodes and caused unexpected cache coldness.
[15:50] Anya: So rollout semantics plus cache TTL caused this.
[15:54] Priya: Exactly — small canaries on cold caches can create noisy results. We suggest warming caches pre-rollout or staging with synthetic traffic.
[16:05] [16:20] Evan: For the pilot, plan: 1) Hosted API pilot with trace sampling and extended retention, 2) Dedicated after baseline and SOC2 signoff. We'll run a replay-driven canary for your most critical route.
[16:34] Maya: Sounds good. Any cost delta for extended trace retention?
[16:38] Evan: Yes there's a small add-on for additional retention and deeper payload storage; we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[16:46] Derek: We need to verify that exported bundles don't include PHI unless we explicitly allow it.
[16:50] Priya: Correct — export default is scrubbed. For private mode you control exports.
[16:58] [17:10] Anya: A quick question on Optimize — can it recommend batching sizes per route?
[17:14] Priya: Yes, Optimize analyzes traffic shapes and suggests batching and quantization profiles; it can also simulate cost impact.
[17:24] Ben: Can Optimize be run on-premise?
[17:28] Priya: We provide an agent that runs locally to gather stats; the recommendations can be consumed locally or via Redwood Dashboard.
[17:38] [17:50] Priya: I'm going to show an integration with Prometheus metrics. You can map trace anomalies to Prom alert rules.
[17:58] Ben: That would help for automated pager deduping.
[18:02] Priya: Yep — mapping is via metrics exporter and label mapping. We'll share a sample helm chart.
[18:10] [18:20] Evan: Quick check — any regulatory controls that would block our pilot?
[18:24] Derek: If PHI enters hosted logs that's a no-go. But with proper redaction and VPC mode it's OK. We need encryption in transit and at rest and KMS control.
[18:36] Evan: Understood. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[18:42] [18:55] Priya: Now final demo piece: show how to search across traces. You can search by correlation id, error code, model variant, or token latency. Typing example now...
[19:10] Anya: Love the free-text search.
[19:14] Priya: Search returns a ranked list and you can bulk-download the top N traces as a diagnostic set.
[19:24] Ben: That will speed our RCA.
[19:28] [19:40] Evan: Ok we're at about 20 minutes in - we have time for a few more deep Qs then wrap with next steps.
[19:48] Maya: Two quick asks — 1) show a replay with PHI redacted, 2) give us a baseline run plan.
[19:56] Priya: We'll prepare a redacted replay and a baseline script for your traffic shapes.
[20:04] Priya: One more thing — sometimes transcription or UI labels say 'K V cache' spaced, or 'kv chache' in older logs, ignore those typos; the underlying keys are consistent.
[20:18] [20:30] Ben: Are there any gotchas migrating from our current in-house inference to Redwood?
[20:34] Evan: Common gotchas: misaligned TTLs, rollout warming, and not tuning kernel hints. Also tokenization differences can cause subtle drift; we'll run an eval suite to surface differences.
[20:50] Anya: Tokenization drift — do you support tokenizer parity with our current models?
[20:54] Priya: We support uploading your tokenizer artifacts or selecting from common tokenizers to match. We'll include the tokenizer parity check in the pilot.
[21:06] [21:20] Priya: Time check — 27 minutes left. Any other critical blockers?
[21:24] Maya: Procurement will want a sample contract and pricing.
[21:27] Evan: We'll send a preliminary SOW and pricing tier for pilot.
[21:32] Derek: Also want to schedule a security deep-dive with your security lead next week.
[21:36] Evan: I'll coordinate.
[21:40] [21:50] Priya: Wrapping up, I recorded the diagnostic bundle and flagged candidate cause as cache thrash + rollout warming. I'll run the 24h replay benchmark and share results.
[21:58] Priya: Action items — Evan send security docs, Priya run benchmarks, Anya provide payloads.
[22:06] Maya: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[22:10] Evan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
[22:18] [22:30] Meeting end.
